I've been farming this land for 15 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent, the well gives me enough water most years, but I have to be careful not to over-pump in dry spells. My main system is wheat-maize — that's the backbone, 20 mu of my land cycling between the two every season. The rest I split among my cash crops.

**Wheat:** I plant in mid-October after the summer maize comes off. I use Jimai 22 — an improved variety, not hybrid, but reliable and the seed station nearby sells it. I base-dress phosphorus and potassium before planting, then top-dress urea at jointing. I irrigate before sowing, at jointing, and at heading — three times is usually enough with a good well. Two or three pesticide sprays: one herbicide early, one for aphids at heading.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June, I go straight in with no-till. Xianyu 335 hybrid — yields well and stands up to the wind. I put nitrogen on in two splits. Usually two irrigations unless July is really dry, then three. Two pesticide passes — one for corn borer, one herbicide.

**Garlic:** 8 mu is my biggest cash earner besides grain. I plant my own saved cloves in October. Deep ploughing first, then heavy fertilizer — garlic needs it. Five irrigations through winter and spring. Four pesticide applications — purple blotch and stem rot are the problems I watch for.

**Stevia:** The contract buyer comes every year, so I know I can sell it. 8 mu, transplanted in spring. Not too hungry for nitrogen — too much and you get leaves but low stevioside content, the buyer docks you for that. I've learned to keep N moderate.

**Cabbage:** 5 mu in autumn. Hybrid seed — heads up faster and more uniform. The market wants uniform heads. Fairly heavy irrigation and some pesticide for caterpillars and aphids.

**Chili:** 5 mu in spring. I grow a local red variety, sell fresh to traders who come to the village. Chili needs the most spraying of anything I grow — mites, aphids, blight. Six pesticide applications is normal for me.

**Onion:** 4 mu in spring. Steady market, not glamorous. Improved variety from the seed shop. Straightforward to grow, fewer problems than chili.
